criteria.slope: (third window median - first window median) / 10 minutes

qualification: No claim of leak freedom; all three runs fail the predefined plateau criterion

diagnosis.confirmed: Growth is in WebView2; host and renderWorker window medians are stable
diagnosis.unresolved: No function-level retaining path or allocation trace. Heap and DOM counters show collection; they do not distinguish native renderer caches from retained allocations.
diagnosis.next: Collect renderer/native allocation retaining evidence during the same fixed UI workload before selecting a product fix; user runs any further long measurement

cleanup.currentBatch: all three profiles deleted and own PIDs reclaimed
cleanup.previousDeletion: blocked by policy during this chat; retained without bypass

cleanup.cleanupVerificationNote: ownPidsStillAlive is the pid intersection of every pid we ever saw with the machine census after cleanup; newWebview2PidsAfterCleanup lists machine-level msedgewebview2 pids that appeared during the run and are still alive (unrelated apps can create these; none of ours may remain)

limitations: host process did not exit on kill request; leftovers were force-stopped by pid
WorkingSet64 counts shared pages mapped into a process; summing a tree therefore double-counts shared WebView2/OS pages. PrivateMemorySize64 (commit) is the closer additive figure.
WebView2 child processes are recycled by the runtime; a per-pid OS lifetime peak disappears with the process, so tree peaks are sampled (<=200 ms) and cross-checked against per-process peak counters.
Only zinecv-desktop.exe and msedgewebview2.exe members are tracked in samples; a one-shot full descendant scan verifies nothing else was spawned.
Preview was triggered through the same Tauri command the UI uses plus an decode of every returned page; the React viewer's own overhead is not included.
Sampler adds one Win32_Process query per interval; the sampler's own CPU/working set is recorded in rawSamplerMeta.
